_comment: Personnel Security Plan generator. Authored at the Phase 2 assessability floor; pairs with PE (PS-3 screening underwrites PE-2 physical-access authorization), AC (PS-3 screening underwrites AC-2 logical-account authorization), AT (PS-6 access agreements paired with AT-2 awareness training), and SA (PS-7 external-personnel hooks into SA-9 external-service governance). Smallest 800-53 family — 9 base controls and no enhancements at moderate; the rigor is in process documentation rather than tooling.
title: Personnel Security Plan
description: Documents how the system's personnel-security risks are managed across the employee / contractor lifecycle: position risk designation, pre-access screening, termination, transfer, access agreements, external-personnel governance, sanctions, and position descriptions. Covers the controls of the PS family in NIST SP 800-53 r5 and aligns with 5 CFR Part 731 (Suitability), 5 CFR Part 1400 (Designation of National Security Positions), Executive Order 12968 (Access to Classified Information), Federal Investigative Standards (FIS), HSPD-12, and OPM background-investigation policies.
intro_template:
This Personnel Security Plan documents the personnel-security approach for {system_name}. It establishes the practices, criteria, cadences, and roles used to designate position risk, screen personnel before access is granted, manage terminations and transfers, obtain and maintain access agreements, govern external personnel, apply sanctions for security violations, and align position descriptions with security responsibilities.

The scope covers position risk / sensitivity designation per PS-2, personnel screening per PS-3, terminations per PS-4, transfers per PS-5, access agreements per PS-6, external personnel per PS-7, sanctions per PS-8, and position descriptions per PS-9 within the {system_name} authorization boundary. The plan is consistent with NIST SP 800-53 r5 (Personnel Security family), 5 CFR Part 731 (Suitability), and the Federal Investigative Standards.
approach_template:
{system_name} relies on {hr_partner_role} for personnel-security workflow execution and {screening_provider} for background-investigation services. Position risk is designated per {position_risk_authority} using the criteria in §4.2. Personnel are screened to the levels in §4.3 before access is granted; screenings are reauthorized on the cadence in §4.3. Terminations, transfers, and external-personnel access follow the workflows in §4.4 through §4.7. Sanctions for security violations are administered per {sanctions_authority}.

Additional details on position risk designation, screening, termination, transfer, access agreements, external personnel, sanctions, and position descriptions are captured in the sub-sections below.
continuous_monitoring_template: Personnel-security performance for {system_name} is tracked through the metrics in §6.1 (active-screening currency rate, termination-revocation SLA compliance, access-agreement currency rate, transfer-rescreening completion rate, sanctions issued, external-personnel attestation completion). The personnel roster is reconciled with system access lists on the cadence in §6.2; gaps surface terminated personnel still holding access (a recurring audit finding when not actively monitored). Continuous Vetting (CV) status — for federal personnel under 5 CFR Part 731 — is monitored through the federal CV system; flag events trigger PE-2 / AC-2 access reviews.
integration_template: This Personnel Security Plan does not stand alone. The PE family inherits PS-3 screening as the prerequisite for PE-2 physical-access authorization; the AC family inherits PS-3 / PS-4 / PS-5 outcomes as the lifecycle of AC-2 logical accounts; the AT family delivers PS-6 access-agreement training and the awareness program PS-8 sanctions reference; the SA family treats external personnel via PS-7 / SA-9 external-service governance; the IR family escalates security violations into the PS-8 sanctions workflow. The following cross-references identify the specific artifacts and locations where PS-related content is exchanged with other RMF deliverables.

commonly_inheritable_controls.from: Organizational position-designation methodology / OPM Position Designation System
Organizational background-investigation program (federal: OPM / NBIB / DCSA)

family_questions.label: Approach basics
family_questions.description: Roles and providers that anchor the rest of the plan.

questions.label: HR partner role (one-liner)
questions.help: Role that owns the personnel-security workflow on the HR side (e.g., 'Personnel Security Branch within HR', 'Agency PSO under the CSO').

questions.label: Background-investigation provider
questions.help: Provider conducting background investigations (e.g., 'OPM / NBIB / DCSA for federal positions', 'HireRight + private references for contractor-only positions').

questions.label: Position-risk designation authority
questions.help: Role / methodology used to designate position risk (e.g., 'OPM Position Designation Tool with HR-CSO joint review', 'Internal position-sensitivity matrix based on data access level').

questions.label: Sanctions-administration authority
questions.help: Role responsible for applying sanctions for security violations (e.g., 'HR with CSO concurrence', 'CO / contracting officer for contractor staff').

questions.label: Access-agreement storage location
questions.help: Where signed access agreements (NDAs, Rules of Behavior, AUPs) are stored. HRMS, contract file, secure document repository.

family_questions.label: Position Risk Designation (PS-2)
family_questions.description: How positions are categorized for screening level.

questions.label: Designation methodology
options: Agency-specific matrix derived from OPM tool
Internal three-tier (Low / Moderate / High) based on system access

questions.label: Risk levels in use
options: National Security Special Sensitive (Tier 5 + SCI eligibility)

questions.label: Designation-review cadence (PS-2 ODV)
questions.help: How often position-risk designations are reviewed (typical: 'Annual + on position-description change'). PS-2 ODV.

questions.label: Designation-review role
questions.help: Role accountable for periodic review of position-risk designations.

questions.label: Mapping from risk level to screening type
questions.help: Crosswalk from each risk level to the corresponding background-investigation type (e.g., 'Low Risk → Tier 1; Moderate Risk Public Trust → Tier 2; High Risk Public Trust → Tier 4').

questions.label: Pre-access screening required for
options: Contractor staff without system access (escorted only)
Foreign nationals (with special handling per EO 12968)

questions.label: Reauthorization cadence
questions.help: When screenings must be redone (e.g., 'Tier 5: every 5 years; Tier 4: every 5 years; Tier 2: every 10 years; or upon Continuous Vetting flag event'). Reference Federal Investigative Standards.

questions.label: Continuous Vetting (CV) participation
options: Yes — federal CV via DCSA Trusted Workforce 2.0
Yes — internal CV beyond federal program

questions.label: Interim-access criteria
questions.help: When and how interim access is granted while full investigation is in progress. Common criteria: favorable fingerprint result + signed SF-86 + supervisor approval.

family_questions.label: Personnel Termination (PS-4)
family_questions.description: Off-boarding workflow that cuts access and recovers assets.

questions.label: Access-revocation SLA
questions.help: Time from termination effective date until logical and physical access is revoked. PS-4 ODV. Common: 'Same business day for involuntary; end-of-business-day for voluntary'.

questions.label: Termination workflow steps
options: Recover GFE laptop / mobile / hardware tokens

questions.label: Involuntary-termination handling
questions.help: Special handling for terminations for cause (immediate access cut prior to notification, escort during exit, asset-recovery procedure).

questions.label: Termination-evidence retention
questions.help: How long termination-checklist evidence is retained (typically per NARA records-retention schedule for personnel records).

family_questions.label: Personnel Transfer (PS-5)
family_questions.description: Reassignment workflow that updates access entitlements.

questions.label: Access-review SLA on transfer
questions.help: Time from transfer effective date until access entitlements are reviewed and adjusted. Common: 'Within 7 days of effective date'.

questions.label: Temporary dual-access policy
questions.help: Whether and how a transferring employee retains access to the old role during transition. Time limit, justification, removal trigger.

questions.label: Screening review on transfer
questions.help: Whether the new role requires a higher-tier screening; trigger for upgrade investigation.

family_questions.label: Access Agreements (PS-6)
family_questions.description: Documents personnel sign before access is granted.

questions.label: Required agreements
options: Acceptable Use Policy / Rules of Behavior
HIPAA Business Associate Agreement (if PHI handled)

questions.label: Agreement-renewal cadence (PS-6 ODV)
questions.help: How often agreements are reviewed / re-signed. PS-6 ODV. Common: 'Annual', 'On significant change to terms'.

questions.label: Storage practice
questions.help: Where signed agreements are stored, retention period, who has read access. Reference NARA records schedule.

questions.label: Completion-tracking mechanism
questions.help: How current-agreement status is tracked (HRMS field, separate compliance dashboard, expiration alerts).

family_questions.label: External Personnel (PS-7)
family_questions.description: Contractor staff, vendor staff, partner-organization staff.

questions.label: Screening requirement for external
questions.help: What background screening external personnel must complete (typically same standard as employees in equivalent risk positions). Reference contract clauses (DFARS 252.204-7012 for DoD).

questions.label: Contract clauses required
options: Notification of personnel changes within N business days

questions.label: Personnel-change notification SLA
questions.help: Time within which external organization must notify the agency of personnel changes (terminations, transfers, new staff requiring access).

questions.label: Periodic external attestation cadence
questions.help: How often external organizations attest to current screening / agreement status (e.g., 'Quarterly').

questions.label: Sanction-decision authority
questions.help: Who decides what sanction applies. Mix of HR, security, supervisor, contracting officer for contractors.

questions.label: Notification process
questions.help: How affected parties are notified, due-process steps, appeal mechanism. Reference org HR policy.

questions.label: Reporting to leadership
questions.help: Cadence at which sanctions are summarized to senior leadership (anonymous trends or named per HR policy).

family_questions.label: Position Descriptions (PS-9)
family_questions.description: Security responsibilities written into position descriptions.

questions.label: Security responsibilities in PDs
options: Role-specific security duties (per AT-3 role-based training)

questions.label: PD-review cadence
questions.help: How often position descriptions are reviewed for currency (typical: 'Annually'). PS-9 ODV.

questions.label: PD-template location
questions.help: Where the standard PD template (with security clauses) lives.

family_questions.label: Personnel Scope and Coverage
family_questions.description: Quantitative scope numbers that anchor metrics later in the plan.

questions.label: Total personnel in scope
questions.help: Approximate count of all personnel (employees + contractors) in scope.

questions.label: Contractor percentage (approximate)
questions.help: Approximate % of total personnel that are contractor / vendor staff.

questions.label: High-risk position count
questions.help: Count of positions designated High Risk Public Trust or higher.

questions.label: External organizations in scope (PS-7)
questions.help: Count of external organizations (contractors, partners, vendors with system access).

family_questions.label: Personnel-Security Metrics & KPIs
family_questions.description: Metrics tracked to demonstrate PS control effectiveness.

questions.label: Tracked metrics
suggestions: % Personnel with current PS-6 access agreement
Mean time from termination effective to access cut (hours)
Sanctions issued per quarter (by category, anonymized)
Continuous-vetting flag events processed within SLA
Position-description currency rate (% reviewed in last cycle)
Open POA&M items linked to PS controls

family_questions.label: Personnel-to-Access Reconciliation
family_questions.description: Continuous verification that personnel records match access entitlements.

questions.label: Reconciliation cadence
questions.help: How often the personnel system (HRMS) is reconciled against logical (AC-2) and physical (PE-2) access lists. Common: 'Weekly automated; monthly manual review'.

questions.label: Gap-handling SLA
questions.help: Time from identification of a reconciliation gap to closure (e.g., 'Same business day for terminated personnel still holding access'). Common audit finding when not actively monitored.

family_questions.label: Cross-references to other RMF artifacts
family_questions.description: Where this plan plugs into the broader RMF package.

questions.label: SSP section reference
questions.help: Where in the SSP the PS control implementations are summarized (e.g., 'SSP §13.10').

questions.label: POA&M ID prefix for PS findings
questions.help: Convention for PS-related POA&M items (e.g., 'POAM-PS-' for general).

questions.label: PE handoff
questions.help: How PS-3 screening status feeds PE-2 physical-access authorization. Trigger that updates PE-2 list when screening lapses or terminates.

questions.label: AC handoff
questions.help: How PS-3 / PS-4 / PS-5 outcomes drive AC-2 logical-account lifecycle. Termination automation, transfer review trigger.

questions.label: AT handoff
questions.help: How PS-6 access agreements pair with AT-2 awareness training. Co-administered or separate?

questions.label: SA handoff
questions.help: How PS-7 external-personnel governance ties to SA-9 external-system-services management. Personnel-change notification flowing through both pathways.

questions.label: IR handoff
questions.help: How security incidents involving personnel feed PS-8 sanctions workflow. Insider-threat reporting.

questions.label: CA-7 continuous-monitoring strategy reference
questions.help: Pointer to the CA-7 monitoring strategy document tying PS continuous-monitoring metrics to the broader ConMon plan.

glossary.definition: A signed acknowledgment of obligations and rules that personnel must adhere to as a condition of system access. Per PS-6. Includes NDAs, Rules of Behavior, AUPs.
An inquiry conducted to determine an individual's suitability for federal employment or eligibility for access to classified information. Per Federal Investigative Standards.
An ongoing process of monitoring eligible personnel for issues that may affect their continued suitability or eligibility, replacing periodic-reinvestigation cycles. Per Trusted Workforce 2.0.
Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency — current federal background-investigation provider, successor to NBIB.
Executive Order 12968 (Access to Classified Information) — establishes uniform criteria and procedures for granting personnel access to classified information.
Standards for the investigations required to determine eligibility for various levels of federal access (Tier 1-5).
Government-Furnished Equipment — equipment provided by the government for use by employees and contractors.
Human Resources Management System — the system of record for personnel data; typically the source-of-truth for PS-2 / PS-3 status.
A threat originating from a person with authorized access who uses that access to harm the organization. CISA-aligned programs coordinate with PS-8 sanctions.
National Agency Check with Inquiries — legacy investigation type, replaced by Tier 1 under FIS.
National Background Investigations Bureau — predecessor to DCSA for federal background investigations.
Office of Personnel Management — federal agency administering personnel policies and the Position Designation System.
Personal Identity Verification card / Common Access Card — federal smart-card credentials whose issuance depends on PS-3 screening.
Per PS-2, the assignment of a risk / sensitivity level to a position based on the duties and access involved. Drives the required investigation tier.
Personnel Security Officer — role responsible for personnel-security workflow at an organization.
Per PS-3, the periodic redetermination of an individual's eligibility for continued access. Now usually achieved through Continuous Vetting rather than periodic reinvestigation.
A document signed by personnel describing acceptable use of system resources and security responsibilities. Common form of PS-6 access agreement.
Standard Form 86 — Questionnaire for National Security Positions; submitted as part of background investigations for sensitive positions.
Standard Form 312 — Classified Information Nondisclosure Agreement; required for personnel granted access to classified information.
Per 5 CFR Part 731, fitness for federal employment based on character or conduct. Distinct from clearance, which is for classified-information access.
Federal Investigative Standards investigation tiers, replacing legacy NACI / MBI / BI. Tier 1 (Low Risk) through Tier 5 (Critical Sensitive National Security).
Federal initiative modernizing the personnel-vetting process, including Continuous Vetting and consolidation of investigation tiers.
Per PS-8, formal disciplinary actions taken in response to security-policy violations. Range from retraining to termination and criminal referral.
